parsed.explanation: Adult alone: birth-marker passport/visa refusal, facility-ID checks, federal/state facility exclusion, and possible short jail plus birth-sex custody create severe exposure. Immigration and prison custody documents hormone removal, solitary, beatings and sexual abuse, raising severity if detained. Adult with minor is lower still: care bans, mandated deadnaming, school investigation, child-welfare scrutiny, sports exclusion and guardian legal jeopardy attach to outing. Some courts, legal aid, local protections and national hate-crime/employment law mediate, but they do not cancel operative hostile entry, facility, custody and minor-care rules. Violence is dated and lacks baseline, so it does not dominate. High risk, severe after discovery, below execution/certain long imprisonment.

entry_documents.exposure: Federal rules bar self-selected passports/visas, eliminate X for new issues, and instruct officers to refuse cases when documents or evidence cast doubt on sex; suspected material misrepresentation can trigger permanent inadmissibility. Trans travellers report passports confiscated/blocked and stranding; same applies to minor documents.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports remain valid; litigation, legal-aid guidance and some court challenges contest parts of the regime.
entry_documents.interaction: Document mismatch can move a traveller into secondary screening, visa denial or fraud adjudication, then possible detention or removal.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Documented immigration custody harms transgender men: forced labour, beatings, solitary and sexual abuse. Federal corrections policies include forced hair cuts, hormone removal and psychiatric drugging. In criminalising states, facility refusal can cause arrest, short jail and men’s-ward placement.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: National hate-crime law, some courts and city ordinances can intervene, but no operative traveller immunity.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: A border or facility stop can become custody, where birth-marker placement, hormone denial and immigration abuse multiply harm; minor care may trigger investigation.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Federal order bars transgender people from government-funded single-sex facilities. Division law requires birth-cert restrooms in schools, universities, prisons and state buildings, with enforcement and ID checks; other mapped state bans cover private spaces or criminalize trespass.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Some states/cities protect gender identity, and 29 mapped states lack facility bans, but those protections do not cancel federal or division restrictions where visited.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Federal facility rules and state birth-cert law operate together: being outed in a public space can produce refusal, questioning, trespass or institutional investigation.

care_services.exposure: Minors face bans on gender-affirming care, funding and insurance restrictions, teacher/social-transition prosecution, child-welfare directives and records subpoenas. Adult care is uncertain: HRT continuity, emergency wards and hormone removal in custody are possible harms.
care_services.protection: No operative traveller-facing care protection documented; some private providers, legal aid or court orders may help.
care_services.interaction: A minor or guardian seeking care can become investigated; care denial interacts with detention, records requests and emergency treatment.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: National agencies treat gender identity as forbidden ideology, direct investigations of schools and teachers, and name radical pro-transgender politics in counterterrorism priorities. Division lacks gender-identity nondiscrimination and bias-crime coverage; majorities support birth-marker laws.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: National employment and hate-crime protections, court challenges and some city ordinances remain, but are partial and uneven.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Threat framing turns routine facility, school or care interactions into police/investigative risk, especially for minors and affirming guardians.

minors_guardians.exposure: Trans minor visitors face care denial, school deadnaming, sports/facility exclusion, child-welfare investigations and possible guardian criminal or custody exposure if seeking affirming care. Guardian can be outed or investigated for failure to report.
minors_guardians.protection: No operative protection documented; local city nondiscrimination and litigation may help only in limited settings.
minors_guardians.interaction: Minor identity/facility issues feed entry screening, school enforcement, health records subpoenas and family services; adult guardian risk rises with child risk.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: State-specific violence is not documented with current baseline; national absolute counts of trans women killed are dated and lack general-homicide context, so they do not establish a current campaign. Official hostility may increase refusal or humiliation.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime law and some local protections exist, but state gender-identity coverage is absent and prosecutions rare.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: If attacked, police may enforce document/facility rules rather than protect; reporting can expose traveller status.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Unanswered: current enforcement frequency, state-specific violence rate, marker-renewal rules, outcome of school investigation, private-provider refusals and whether courts block federal restrictions.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Legal-aid FAQ, civil-liberties litigation and some enjoined orders may mitigate, but protection is not shown to operate for travellers.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Regime status changes by date and division; unknowns prevent assuming safety, while ongoing litigation may reduce some exposures.

anchor_checks.comparison: Near: birth-marker documents, facility pressure, detention-like checks and fines, no execution; lower because immigration custody abuse, minor-care criminalization and guardian exposure are added; higher because no weekly support-centre raids or broad pretrial custody.

Clearly lower: visitor exclusion and humiliation without birth-sex custody, hormone removal, sexual-abuse reports, or criminalized care/school outing. This dossier combines federal and division facility enforcement with severe custody and minor harms.

Higher: not routine indefinite detention, torture, or credible capital consequence; but border/facility custody, immigration abuse and men’s-ward placement overlap enough to sit just above 0.15-B, near the low end of High Risk.

parsed.synthesis: The operative exposure is layered, not optional: passport/visa mismatch can trigger refusal or fraud adjudication, while federal and division facility rules make birth-marker compliance a condition of public restrooms, schools, prisons and many funded spaces. Outing by an ID check can escalate to trespass, detention, hormone denial and custody abuse. Adult travellers alone face severe but not catastrophic consequences; minors and affirming guardians face additional criminalized care, school outing, child-welfare and immigration/fraud risk. Partial remedies and hostile institutions make violence uncertain; the regime is unsafe but below imprisonment-execution extremes.
